title: Machine learning inside a required data science course
summary: Across five observed editions, Edinburgh places INFR08030 in the second-year compulsory group. Its description includes supervised machine learning, inference and algorithmic bias. The separate INFR10086 Machine Learning course remains an option.
facts: Observed editions: 2022/23–2026/27; five editions | Whole-course credit: 20 SCQF credits | Requirement: Second-year compulsory course
notes: The credits belong to the whole course, not exclusively to AI. Annual catalogue versions are not one entry cohort; teaching, student uptake and learning outcomes were not measured.

title: A listed project option can have a non-delivery notice
summary: Edinburgh lists SDP and EIP in a choose-20-credit project group through 2025/26, while the 2025/26 EIP page says it is not being delivered. In 2026/27, SDP is separately compulsory, with an approved Formula Student substitution route; EIP retains its non-delivery notice.
facts: Project group: 2023/24–2025/26 | SDP separately compulsory again: 2026/27 | EIP non-delivery notice observed: 2025/26 and 2026/27
notes: Programme eligibility and delivery notices are different facts. A yearly notice does not establish permanent closure or actual teaching. The 2026/27 EIP page was retrieved again on 3 November 2026; it is not the earlier saved byte version.

title: MIT teaching plans mention LLMs before the latest catalogue sentence
summary: The official-linked Fall 2025 6.1040 course site already plans LLM-assisted design, coding and application agents, while the Fall 2025 Registrar description lacks that sentence. The verified 2026/27 central catalogue explicitly mentions LLM design and coding.
facts: Course: 6.1040 Software Design | Earlier term-specific plan: Fall 2025 | Latest central catalogue: 2026/27
notes: This establishes public plans at different document levels, not first classroom adoption. The 2025/26 annual programme rules remain missing. The latest catalogue has a 15-versus-18-unit discrepancy between tables; 6.1040 is a conditional option, not universally required.

title: A machine learning description changes its organizing emphasis
summary: MIT 6.3900 changes from prediction-oriented wording in 2023/24 to an optimization-oriented description in 2024/25, explicitly listing supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning. The core wording continues in the Fall 2025 Registrar archive and 2026/27 catalogue.
facts: Course: 6.3900 | Observed wording interval: 2023/24 → 2024/25 | Course total: 12 MIT units in the observed versions
notes: New wording does not establish first classroom use or prove that earlier teaching omitted the topic. This course is an option within programme tracks, not an individually required course for every 6-3 student.

title: An AI-list condition needs an applicability check
summary: The verified 2026/27 central MIT 6-3 catalogue requires at least two AUS subjects and at least 12 units from its AI Subjects list. The departmental 6-3_2025 rules page, labelled for entrants from Fall 2025, still specifies Independent Inquiry constraints. These official source layers do not yet establish one rule for an individual student.
facts: Central catalogue condition: At least 12 MIT units from AI Subjects | Comparison editions: 2024/25 → 2026/27 | Decision: Applicability unresolved
notes: The 12 units constrain chosen courses rather than adding 12 units to the programme total, and the list includes broad theoretical subjects. The departmental page was retrieved in 2026 and lists Spring 2027 candidates; it is not a 2025/26 archive.

title: CMU keeps the AI category while changing its options
summary: Five observed CMU editions keep a requirement to choose one course from the AI category, with a minimum of 9 CMU units. The 2025/26 named list includes 07-280 and 10-301 and no longer lists 10-315; 15-281 is still listed then but absent in 2026/27, which includes 16-280.
facts: Observed editions: 2022/23–2026/27 | Category minimum: One course; at least 9 CMU units | 15-281 latest description: Still present in the catalogue
notes: Absence from this category does not establish course closure or general elective ineligibility. Approved unnamed alternatives existed in earlier rules; 15-382 carries a Qatar-only note in the last two editions. Edition labels and entry-cohort applicability differ.

title: More units do not by themselves establish new content
summary: CMU 15-122 and 15-150 each move from 10 units in 2022/23 to 12 units in 2023/24, remaining in the all-required CS core. Their main catalogue descriptions are unchanged after whitespace normalization and removal of separate metadata fields. Both retain 12 units through 2026/27.
facts: Courses: 15-122 and 15-150 | Units per course: 10 → 12 CMU units | Observed change: 2022/23 → 2023/24
notes: The comparison covers main descriptions, not assignments, prerequisites or classroom delivery. Institutional credit systems are not converted or summed across universities.

title: A broad mathematics list becomes two separate groups
summary: UW–Madison CS BS changes its additional mathematics requirement from two courses in a broad list to one Linear Algebra choice and one Probability or Statistics choice in 2024/25. Both groups remain in 2025/26 and 2026/27.
facts: Observed change: 2023/24 → 2024/25 | Earlier minimum: Two courses; at least 6 credits | Continuing options: MATH 340 and STAT 324
notes: These courses are options within groups, not individually compulsory. MATH 375 substitution and duplicate-credit restrictions still apply. Historical Guide pages are summer archives; the comparison does not identify the approval date or affected entry cohort.

title: R becomes explicit in a statistics course description
summary: UW–Madison STAT 324 adds an explicit R-programming statement in the 2024/25 description while retaining its earlier statistics topics. That statement remains in 2025/26 and 2026/27; the course stays an option in the CS mathematics requirement.
facts: Observed wording interval: 2023/24 → 2024/25 | Course: STAT 324 | Whole-course credit: 3 UW–Madison credits
notes: Wording establishes neither first classroom use of R nor three credits devoted solely to R. Historical pages are summer archives. The 2026/27 page was retrieved again on 3 November 2026, with the relevant wording and credit checked.

title: An explicit alternative can document an existing permission
summary: Waterloo BCS names CS 240 or CS 240E and CS 241 or CS 241E explicitly in its 2023/24 programme table. The 2022/23 course catalogue already allowed the enriched courses to replace the standard courses wherever required. The explicit alternatives persist through 2026/27.
facts: Programme wording change: 2022/23 → 2023/24 | Existing substitution evidence: 2022/23 course catalogue | Pairs checked: CS 240/240E and CS 241/241E
notes: The wording change is not evidence that the courses or substitution rights were newly created. Entry, prerequisite and offering conditions remain relevant; this finding is limited to these two pairs.

title: Non-mathematics electives are reorganized in Waterloo BCS
summary: The 2025/26 BCS still uses the earlier breadth-and-depth structure. The 2026/27 version organizes 4.0 elective units into a 1.0 + 1.0 + 2.0 distribution, including at least 1.0 unit at the 200 level or above and no double counting with the degree communication requirement. Both retain at least 5.0 non-mathematics units and two communication courses.
facts: Narrowed version interval: 2025/26 → 2026/27 | Reorganized elective subset: 4.0 Waterloo units | Parent minimum retained: At least 5.0 non-mathematics units
notes: The first 1.0 unit is from Arts or BET/BUS/COMM/STV; the next 1.0 is from Environment/Health/Science; the remaining 2.0 uses those ranges. These are observed document versions, not exact implementation dates or proof of outcomes.

title: Toronto changes which courses count within an unchanged total
summary: The St George CS Major keeps its 3.0-credit Later years module while narrowing its 200-level CSC list in 2024/25 to CSC209H1, CSC299H1 and CSC299Y1. It also explicitly states two separate 0.5-credit caps, for CSC412H1/STA414H1 and CSC438H1/MAT309H1. These features remain after a later regrouping.
facts: Observed change: 2023/24 → 2024/25 | Major total: 8.0 credits | Later years module: 3.0 credits
notes: Other 200-level courses are not thereby abolished or excluded from all other requirements. Earlier omission of these caps from this paragraph does not override other exclusion rules. Groups A/B/C and other conditions also change in later versions.

title: An existing deep learning course gains a new completion role
summary: Toronto adds CSC302H1 and CSC413H1 to the CS Major integrative inquiry-based activity list in 2023/24. Both courses already existed in 2022/23, when CSC413H1 already described deep learning. Their main descriptions are unchanged across that interval, and both remain listed as options through 2026/27.
facts: Observed approval-list change: 2022/23 → 2023/24 | Courses: CSC302H1 and CSC413H1 | Requirement role: Optional route to the integrative activity
notes: Other courses and ASIP provide alternatives. This is not a new-course count or a compulsory AI-credit claim. Historical PEY transition rules and actual teaching were not adjudicated.
